products.name: Modernizing Office 365 Connector Workflows to Microsoft Graph (Logic Apps / Power Automate) — Commercial
products.short_description: A whole estate of Office 365 connector flows that can't use managed identity or are aging out — this program inventories them and migrates them to managed-identity Microsoft Graph workflows, at scale.
products.description:
A whole estate of Office 365 connector flows that can't use managed identity or are aging out — this program inventories them and migrates them to managed-identity Microsoft Graph workflows, at scale.

One workflow hitting the Office 365 connector's authentication wall is a fix; dozens of them is a program. Organizations accumulate Logic Apps and Power Automate flows built on the Office 365 Outlook/Users/Excel connectors, all authenticated as a user or service account — no managed identity, standing credentials, and mounting operational risk. This solution is the migration program: inventory every connector-based flow and its auth, classify by risk and Graph-migratability, and systematically re-platform them onto managed-identity Microsoft Graph workflows — with a repeatable per-flow playbook, a pilot-first rollout, and parity validation so nothing silently breaks in the cutover.

Run it yourself — simpler, cheaper, and proven

You do not need a consultant. The package hands you the field-tested method as self-guided, click-by-click documentation a competent admin can follow end to end — backed by ready-to-run PowerShell.

  • Simpler — exact, ordered steps with full navigation paths; every object you create is named and reused through testing and troubleshooting.
  • Cheaper — one fixed price instead of an open meter; a comparable consulting engagement runs well into the thousands per day. Reusable on every rollout.
  • Tested — a pilot-first method (Assess → Configure → Pilot → Validate → Expand) with explicit pass/fail gates.

What's inside

  • Inventory — enumerate Logic Apps / Power Automate flows using Office 365 connectors and how each authenticates (user vs service account vs secret)
  • Classify — score each flow by risk (standing credentials, over-scope) and by how cleanly it maps to a Graph + managed-identity design
  • Per-flow playbook — the repeatable pattern to re-platform a connector flow onto managed-identity Graph (leans on #1/#2/#3/#5; points to #4 for scoping)
  • Pilot-first rollout — migrate a pilot cohort, validate parity, then wave the rest with rollback per flow
  • Govern the end state — prevent regression to connector-based auth, with a validation script reporting remaining connector/credential usage

The repeatable way

Every solution follows the same repeatable shape, so each deployment feels familiar and low-risk — buy once, reuse the playbook for the next wave and the next project.

The bottom line

An at-scale migration of Office 365 connector workflows onto managed-identity Microsoft Graph — inventoried, risk-ranked, migrated with a repeatable playbook, and validated for parity so the estate ends credential-free.

What you receive — every file in your download

This package is delivered as downloadable files you keep and reuse across unlimited devices — nothing is left out and nothing else is required:

  • Implementation Guide (PDF) — the complete, click-by-click solution: solution overview, requirements, step-by-step implementation, testing & validation, troubleshooting, best practices.
  • PowerShell Scripts (ZIP) — 5 ready-to-run scripts (read-only discovery/validation/reporting; remediation defaults to a safe preview):
    • O365GRAPH-Classify.ps1 — score each discovered connector flow by risk and Graph-migratability
    • O365GRAPH-Discovery.ps1 — inventory Azure Logic Apps that use Office 365 connectors and record
    • O365GRAPH-Report.ps1 — program dashboard: total connector flows, migrated, remaining, and risk
    • O365GRAPH-Set-AppRole.ps1 — assign (or verify) a Microsoft Graph application app-role on a
    • O365GRAPH-Validate.ps1 — PASS/FAIL check that a migrated flow uses a managed identity + Microsoft

Delivered as a Word document and PDF, plus all five PowerShell scripts in a single ZIP — yours to keep and reuse.
